grammar.title: 7B: Second conditional — talking about dreams
grammar.explanation:
We use the second conditional for dreams and wishes. They are not real now.

Form: **If** + past simple, **would** + verb. I run every day. If I ran in the morning, I would feel great.

After **If I**, we often use **were**: If I were rich, I would buy a big ball.

First conditional is for real plans: **If I play well, I will win**. Second is for dreams: **If I played in a big game, I would win**.
examples: *If I had a new ball*, I *would play* with my friends. (a dream)
*If I were* the winner, I *would* be very happy. (not real now)
*If we played* every day, we *would win* more games. (a wish)
*If I could run* faster, I *would win* the race. (impossible now)

practice.q: Fill in: If I ___ (have) more time, I would play football every day.
Which sentence is a dream? A) If I play, I will win. B) If I played, I would win.
practice.a: B. It is not real now.
